Measured (3 seeds each, all complete, none feasible):
E001 9 ep: acc 0.7430, 9.43 s. E002 10 ep: acc 0.7495, 10.55 s. E003 compiled 9 ep(?)/10 ep recipe: acc 0.7486, 12.07 s. Compile was slower than eager, a miss: I predicted ~8.5 s.

1. Epoch dial (E001→E002): +0.65 pp/epoch, +1.11 s/epoch (~11.8%/epoch). The implied fixed cost is near zero or negative, so nearly all time scales with epochs. That weakens H3 (fixed costs >10%). To reach 0.753 by extrapolation I need about 10.5-11 epochs, ~11.3-12 s. The slope is likely concave, so budget 11 epochs.

2. Compile (E003): time went UP by about 1.5 s versus E002 (10.55 → 12.07) with accuracy about equal (0.7486 vs 0.7495, within noise). Compile or autotune cost leaks into timed code, or the 4-CPU pin makes compile-generated code and dispatch no faster. The measured regularity: systems "optimizations" that add compile are net negative here. H2.2.1 is refuted by E003 as measured. Raw eager is already GPU-bound at ~1.1 s/epoch, so launch overhead is not the bottleneck. I distrust further compile-based ideas (I006 builds on compiled port, which is a worse base).

3. Noise: E003 vs E002 accuracy differ by 0.1 pp, consistent with 3-seed-mean std of ~0.15-0.25 pp. Time noise unmeasured, assumed 1-3%. Sitting at 0.753 on 3 seeds is uncertain by ±0.2 pp.

4. Accuracy tricks (EMA, LS, flip) are unmeasured. A +0.2-0.4 pp gain is worth 0.3-0.6 epoch (~0.4-0.7 s). Changing training dynamics (Muon, progressive resizing) at a tuned lr is likely to lose accuracy; progressive resizing saves FLOPs but at 9 epochs most likely loses more than 0.2 pp.

Unsure: whether the slope stays at 0.65 pp/epoch, whether EMA gives ≥0.2 pp, true time noise, and why compile was slower.

forecasts.reason: EMA every 5 steps is cheap, but in 9 epochs with triangular LR decaying to 0.07 the gain is likely ~0.1-0.3 pp over E001's 0.743; unlikely to cross 0.753.
Identical rerun should land within ~2% time and ~0.2 pp of E002; per-seed std likely ~0.2-0.35 pp.
Compiled base was slower than eager (E003 12.07 s); dropping the ragged batch removes at most a recompile, maybe 0.3-1 s saved, still likely above eager.
Muon without retuning on a tuned SGD backbone is likely lower accuracy at a fixed epoch count; extra Newton-Schulz cost offsets gains.
Low-res early epochs save ~15% time at the cost of >0.2 pp accuracy in a 9-10 epoch schedule, plus cudnn autotune/resize overhead.

cruxes: Does EMA/Lookahead or any cheap accuracy trick give ≥0.3 pp at 9 epochs (convertible into ~0.5 epoch, ~0.6 s)?
Why was the compiled port slower (12.07 s vs 10.55 s): compile leaking into timed code or slower kernels? Eager time per epoch of ~1.1 s may be a GPU-bound floor.
What is the true seed-to-seed and run-to-run noise (I005)? It decides how many epochs (~10.5-11) are needed to be safely over 0.753.
